hero.caption: A Sarajevo Rose is a concrete scar caused by a mortar shell’s explosion that was later filled with red resin. Mortar rounds landing on concrete create a unique fragmentation pattern that looks almost floral in arrangement. The roses are disappearing as the asphalt is replaced.

images.caption: Considered the best-preserved inn in Sarajevo, it dates from 1551. Like all other hans (inns), it has suffered numerous fires. It was rebuilt many times and is now the only one remaining in Sarajevo. It now houses stores, offices, and a restaurant.

images.caption:
Not unlike other Eastern European countries, notably Hungary or Poland, Bosnia too is now merely a shadow of its former glory of rich cultural diversity, with its currently empty synagogues, having been drained of a sizable portion of its brainpower, a victim of unifying and simplifying nationalism.
In the photo, Aškenaška sinagoga - the only functioning synagogue in Sarajevo, in the Moorish Revival (neo-Moorish) style, a popular choice for synagogues in the Austro-Hungarian Empire. [6]
